blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction requires ground truth linking camera motion, surface deformation, material correspondence and image appearance. We introduce the Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark, generated with LumenMorph, an open-source toolkit for creating, annotating and evaluating tubular scenes. The release contains 5,580 RGB images. Its baseline crosses three surface-motion conditions with moving and stationary cameras in six scene families; matched appearance variants cover only moving-camera finite-element actions in four families. Documented public and evaluation interfaces expose camera poses, geometry, depth, deformation fields, persistent material correspondences and discrete finite-element records. Persistent triangle identities and material weights let users track the same surface location across frames and query its three-dimensional trajectory. Separately implemented geometric and mechanical checks assess annotation consistency with the generating models. Structure-from-motion, optical-flow and supplied-geometry displacement-interpolation studies demonstrate how the resource distinguishes registration coverage from geometric accuracy, exposes camera- and surface-motion effects, and tests the benefits and mismatch of mechanical priors. Public readers, evaluation contracts and the configurable generator support reuse and extension. Data integrity, fixed-environment repeatability and retained-prediction score replay have distinct verification scopes. The benchmark provides a controlled synthetic reference without claiming anatomical or clinical realism.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Deformable reconstruction in colonoscopy must distinguish camera motion from
surface motion under limited visibility. A rigid reconstruction accumulated
over time can absorb deformation into biased camera poses or geometry.
Surface similarity alone may also conceal correspondence errors: a nearby
surface point need not be the same material point—a fixed location on the
wall followed as it moves. Evaluation therefore
requires linked observations, material identities, geometry and visibility,
together with explicit assumptions about the motion-generating model.
Known camera poses alone do not resolve the inverse deformation problem.

blocks.en:
The methodological contribution is a benchmark with an explicit, accessible
and checked connection between image observations, camera states, persistent
material identities, deformed geometry and discrete mechanical records. This
integration lets researchers evaluate reconstruction accuracy, material-motion
consistency and surface support under paired acquisition conditions, without
introducing a new reconstruction algorithm. The novelty is the queryable
connection, rather than any one annotation or the use of simulation alone.
The reusable contribution has two parts: the fixed, versioned benchmark,
with linked annotations and separately implemented consistency checks; and
LumenMorph, the open-source generator and reader/evaluation toolkit for
creating and studying additional tubular configurations. Reconstruction,
optical-flow and supplied-geometry mechanical studies illustrate uses of
these resources. They distinguish camera accuracy, sparse geometry, surface
support and registration coverage, while a static phantom control examines
performance on physical imagery under its declared acquisition contract.
The engineered scene families provide controlled reconstruction diagnosis,
not a sampled clinical population.

blocks.en: 1.1 Related work
blocks.zh: 1.1 相关工作

blocks.en:
Existing resources address complementary evaluation needs. SimCol3D provides
a synthetic depth and pose benchmark with separate anatomies for
training and evaluation ( Rau et al., 2024 ) , while RealSynCol expands
CT-derived geometry and image realism ( Lena et al., 2026 ) . C3VD and
C3VDv2 provide phantom images acquired with clinical colonoscopes and
registered dense labels ( Bobrow et al., 2023 ; Golhar et al., 2026 ) .
DynamicColon, the dataset introduced alongside the ColonSplat reconstruction
method by Smolak-Dyżewska et al. (2026) , provides
per-time-step point clouds to evaluate whole-scene motion, beyond appearance
along the observed camera path. C3VD-DEFCOL combines parameterized peristalsis and
centerline motion with depth-conditioned image translation, reporting 110
videos from 11 colon geometries and dense dynamic annotations ( Luk et al., 2026 ) . VR-Caps and SimIntestine
extend simulation to capsule
endoscopy ( Incetan et al., 2021 ; Singh et al., 2025 ) , and SimuScope
incorporates deformable tissues in surgical
simulation ( Martyniak et al., 2025 ) . Dense dynamic annotations and
mechanical simulation are therefore established capabilities. The present
work focuses on their auditable connection to persistent material identity,
controlled acquisitions and reconstruction-pipeline evaluation.

Prior colonoscopy reconstruction methods also motivate this evaluation
setting. Hong et al. used tubular structure to reconstruct virtual colons
from video ( Hong et al., 2014 ) ; Ruano et al. trained shape-from-shading

benefit from benchmarks in which image formation, correspondence and motion
can be examined separately, while clinical transfer is evaluated using
physical data.

blocks.en:
The motivation is to provide controlled acquisition and deformation conditions
for evaluating reconstruction. The distinguishing feature is the explicit,
queryable connection between image observations, persistent surface material
identities, geometric states and discrete mechanical records. A persistent

frames; separate public and evaluator interfaces make ground-truth access
explicit. Discrete loads, responses and energy terms expose the assumptions
behind FE-derived motion. These links allow errors to be examined against
known camera and surface motion while controlling appearance variations.

The appearance add-on, stored as appearance/ in the downloadable dataset, changes how an
existing scene looks while retaining its motion. It reuses only the moving

(package v2), f04 (v11), f05 (v14) and f06 (v17). These are selections from

states under five conditions: diffuse symmetric lighting, diffuse asymmetric
lighting, coated symmetric lighting, and half/double exposure of the diffuse
symmetric radiance. Thus 360 shared truth states and 1,080 traced radiance maps
produce 1,800 RGB images. The compact design selects one originally designated
development family (f01), the validation family (f04), and the two recovery-test
families (f05/f06); it spans straight, singly bent and doubly bent geometry
and both amplitude settings. f02/f03 do not have appearance variants. This
bounded selection preserves the original roles and controls production cost;
it is not an exhaustive anatomy or curvature experiment. f01 remains development, f04 validation and f05/f06
retain their original final-test designation. All conditions were declared
before reconstruction; inspecting this experiment does not leave these scenes
unseen for subsequent reconstruction development.

therefore do not measure absolute-scale recovery.
We write the fitted scale, rotation and translation as ( s , Q , t ) (s,Q,t) .

world and camera bases: with F = diag ⁡ ( 1 , − 1 , 1 ) F=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1) , C ref = F ​ C w C_{\mathrm{ref}}=FC_{w} and R ref = F ​ R w ​ c ​ F R_{\mathrm{ref}}=FR_{wc}F ; geometry uses

Camera-position absolute trajectory error (ATE) is summarized by its root
mean square error (RMSE). For camera-to-world rotations R ^ i , R i \hat{R}_{i},R_{i} ,
absolute orientation error is the angle of R i T ​ Q ​ R ^ i R_{i}^{T}Q\hat{R}_{i} ; relative

registration is not treated as a one-frame increment. Angles use an atan2 expression to retain resolution near zero.

At least three paired centers, nonstationary center spread and a
second/first centered singular-value ratio of 10 − 6 10^{-6} in both trajectories
are required; otherwise the alignment-dependent scores are unavailable.
Local
surface error is the unsigned distance from each retained reconstructed point
to the complete, constant truth mesh for frames 60–74. Surface support is
measured in the reverse direction, from a fixed visible-surface sample to
the nearest reconstructed point. The sample uses every 16th pixel in both
image axes across all 15 local frames, independently of registration success.
Thus point-to-surface error asks whether reconstructed points are close to
the wall, while surface-to-point support asks which visible wall regions have
nearby reconstructed points. Neither measures persistent material
correspondence by itself. A sparse, incomplete model can score well on the
first metric and poorly on the second: a few points on one accurately
reconstructed patch have low point-to-surface distance, while uncovered wall
regions remain far from every point. We report both distributions, point
counts and their tails; a median alone can hide large geometry outliers.
Neither nearest-surface direction establishes correct material identity.

blocks.en:

separately controlled camera and surface motion. We compare a zero-motion

144 image pairs. Selection uses the public suite index and verifies
family, condition and split rather than assuming package numbers.

before inference and scoring.

claiming metrological precision. Supplied C3VD poses are evaluator truth;
no known-pose model is used as image-based inference or as surface truth for
the rectified images.

blocks.en: 4 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
The resource links geometry, persistent material identities, motion and
appearance so that evaluation questions can be posed under known acquisition
conditions. Users can distinguish camera-induced disagreement from prescribed
surface motion, examine whether sparse geometry supports the visible wall,
and test a mechanical assumption with supplied material correspondence.
The fixed release makes these questions accessible without generating a new
dataset; LumenMorph supports extensions within its published configuration
interface. The three usage studies illustrate complementary uses of the same
linked annotations.

检查几何结构是否支持可见的墙壁

blocks.en:
In the SfM study, complete registration does not establish accurate camera
poses or adequate surface reconstruction. Point-to-surface proximity and
visible-wall support answer different questions: small typical distances can
coexist with sparse support or severe outliers. All requested synthetic frames
register and the fixed-profile computational repeats agree exactly, yet global
and local camera errors differ markedly. A reconstructs more local points and
achieves a smaller median visible-surface-to-point distance in every matched
condition, while B has lower surface RMSE in most conditions. Neither profile
dominates all reported measures. Large retained outliers also prevent small
surface medians from establishing uniformly accurate geometry.

在SfM研究中,完整的注册不能建立准确的相机
摆设或适当的地面重建。 近距离和近距离
可见墙支持 回答不同的问题: 小的典型距离可以
与稀少的支持或严重外援共存。 所有要求的合成帧
登记簿和固定标注的重复计算完全一致,但全球
和本地相机误差明显不同。 重建更多局部点
在每个匹配处实现较小的可见-表面-点距离中位数
条件,而B在大多数条件下具有较低的表面RMSE. 没有配置文件
主导所有报告的措施。 大型保留舱门也防止小型
从建立统一准确的几何学的表面中位数。

blocks.en:
The optical-flow study shows how controlled camera and surface motion expose
condition-dependent performance. A learned estimator is not uniformly best
on these inputs. The static stationary arm fixes geometry and camera pose
while retaining photometric perturbations, helping distinguish residual image
variation from geometric motion.

blocks.en:
The mechanical-record study tests an energy prior after supplying geometry,
stiffness and material correspondence. Improved interpolation for compatible
fields and deterioration for prescribed non-FE fields reveal the usefulness
and possible mismatch of that assumption. The motion classes have different
amplitudes, so this is not a causal isolation of mechanical compatibility.
The experiment is a privileged-input resource demonstration rather than
image-based recovery.

僵硬和物质通信。 为兼容性改进插值

和可能的不匹配 这个假设。 运动课不同

实验是特权投入的资源展示,而不是

blocks.en:
The physical-phantom controls complement the synthetic comparison by
retaining reconstruction failures, partial coverage and unidentifiable gauges
on real images. Calibration and preprocessing provenance qualify their
interpretation. Their role is to expose transfer limits under the fixed
profiles. Complete descending registration coexists with 10.2–28.7-degree
mean orientation errors, while transverse registration reaches only 2/61 frames.
These controls do not establish uniformly accurate camera reconstruction,
deformation recovery or a general ranking of the pipelines.

measure computational stability on exposed scenes, not independent anatomical
confirmation. The local experiment observes a fixed deformed wall state;
its small fitted errors do not establish continuous deformation tracking.

blocks.en:
Data consistency, repeatability and score replay answer separate questions.
Geometric/mechanical checks establish agreement with the stated generating

blocks.en: 5 Limitations
blocks.zh: 5 限制

blocks.en:
The dataset contains six engineered scene families, not 18 independent
anatomies. Geometry, texture, camera trajectories and material parameters are
specified by the generator rather than sampled from a clinical population.
The FE model uses linear elasticity and infinitesimal strain; the relative
Green–infinitesimal strain discrepancy reaches 0.145 in the strong-deformation
regime. Numerical equilibrium and positive quadrature-point Jacobians do not
validate tissue mechanics or large-deformation constitutive behavior.
Deformation amplitude also differs between FE and non-FE conditions, so their
comparison cannot isolate mechanical compatibility. Although the baseline
crosses camera mode and surface-motion condition, the appearance extension
covers only four families and moving-camera FE actions. It is not a complete
factorial design, and its findings do not establish interactions across all
camera, motion and appearance combinations.

blocks.en:
The physical controls evaluate global reconstructions of two static phantom
acquisitions. Source-calibrated inputs use the checked PINHOLE remapping of
published omnidirectional calibration, with the interpolation and
lens-model approximations described in Section 2.12 .
Repeatability covers two corrected source derivatives, four synthetic families,
five appearance conditions and three source-calibrated physical image sets, with three executions per group
under the declared source/runtime/CPU profile. The flow comparison covers
three development families and one pretrained RAFT checkpoint. These designs do not
support population-level generalization or clinical performance claims.
The mechanical consumer demonstrates interpolation with supplied stiffness
and material identities, including deterioration under model mismatch; it
does not validate estimation of those inputs or recovery from ordinary images.
The image-only SfM comparisons use no FE prior. Binary agreement within
a fixed profile is not a test of agreement across rebuilds, hardware or thread
settings.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
The Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark provides linked image observations,
camera and surface states, persistent material correspondences and discrete
mechanical annotations. Paired acquisition and appearance conditions,
documented information boundaries and separately implemented consistency
checks support controlled evaluation against the generating models. The usage
studies show why reconstruction accuracy, registration coverage, surface
support and flow must be evaluated separately, and how mechanical records
can expose both benefits and mismatch of a prior. Fixed-environment
repeatability and retained-prediction metric replay remain distinct from
portable end-to-end reproduction.
By releasing both a fixed, validated benchmark and its open-source generator,
this work provides a reusable foundation for evaluating and extending
deformable reconstruction methods in controlled tubular environments.

blocks.en:
The repeatability contract requires three A-SIFT1 executions and three
corrected B global/local mapper repetitions for every primary family and
condition under the frozen one-thread, seed-zero profile. A extracts features
afresh and preserves each extraction database. Matching is inherited only when
all canonical camera, image, keypoint and descriptor schemas, identities, shapes
and payloads equal the corresponding closed matching input exactly; otherwise
it is recomputed. All A mappers are fresh. B inherits its corresponding closed
extraction/matching inputs. A separately implemented direct-row readback verifies every
A reuse decision and all private mapper databases. We compare canonical complete SQLite payloads, every
full-precision binary model file, stage exits, effective native options and actual
registered frame names. Documentary output paths are recorded separately.
This tests repeatability on the complete requested population; a fixed seed
or one successfully repeated example alone is insufficient. Timeouts,
fragments and absent models remain in the denominator. Deterministic data
generation, inference repeatability, coverage and metric replay are separate
properties. The three runs are computational repetitions, not independent
scene observations or a hardware-portability test. The current A-SIFT1 and
corrected B populations use a dedicated 24-core Intel Core Ultra 9 Ubuntu
host with 64 GB RAM. Independent physical groups may execute
concurrently, while the three repetitions within each group remain
sequential. The Ubuntu processor has two core/cache classes. The CPU-AFFINITY1 execution profile restricts every native process
in a three-repeat group to the same single core from the homogeneous
eight-core class, including its children. Runtime receipts retain the actual CPU sets and effective options.
The hardware-blocking control is described above.
The one-thread numerical profile is unchanged. Host differences
and resource contention preclude a comparative wall-clock speed claim.

blocks.en:
The following complete example saves a zero-displacement control using only
public image dimensions, then opens privileged truth to query the same
material points at frames 52 and 53 and score the already saved prediction.
The baseline reader returns BGR channel order; only its shape is used here.
This control demonstrates the interface and is not a trained reconstruction
method or an additional scientific comparison. import os
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from backend.src.benchmark_reader import PublicDataset, EvaluationDataset
from backend.src.benchmark_evaluate import evaluate

package = Path(os.environ[’SDTUBE_DATA’]) / ’benchmark/v2’
output = Path(os.environ[’SDTUBE_OUT’])
output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
public = PublicDataset(package)
# Freeze a zero-motion control using only the public image shape.
height, width = public.rgb(52, ’moving’).shape[:2]
prediction = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.float64)
np.savez_compressed(output / ’prediction.npz’, prediction=prediction)

# Privileged inspection begins only after the prediction has been saved.
truth = EvaluationDataset(package)
dense = truth.dense(52, ’moving’)
ids = dense[’triangle_id’][dense[’valid’]][::4096]
weights = dense[’material_barycentric’][dense[’valid’]][::4096]
x52 = truth.material_points(ids, weights, 52, ’moving’)
x53 = truth.material_points(ids, weights, 53, ’moving’)
print(’Queried material points:’, len(ids))
print(’First point displacement:’, x53[0] - x52[0])
scores = evaluate(package, output / ’prediction.npz’, output / ’scores.json’,
                  task=’displacement’, frame=52, target=53, stream=’moving’,
                  coordinate_frame=’benchmark-world’)
print(scores[’primary’]) The query uses immutable triangle IDs and barycentric weights from the source
frame, so x53-x52 follows the same material, including points that may
be invisible later. The scorer evaluates every source-valid surface pixel;
the sparse inspection query does not select the scored population. The JSON
records coverage, conditional/full-population errors and input hashes. Its
world-frame declaration specifies axes and scene units; the scorer fits no
transform or scale to truth. A real method must save its own prediction before
privileged inspection, use only its declared inference inputs and retain
missing outputs in coverage. Prediction shape is native H × W × 3 H\times W\times 3 ;
other tasks and appearance-specific availability follow the main article.
